newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU to face barley subsidy pressure.
newsitem.headline: EU to face barley subsidy pressure.

text.p: The European Union is likely to come under pressure to grant substantial barley export subsidies following Saudi Arabia's purchase of about 1.4 million tonnes on world markets, traders said on Tuesday.

Exporters bidding to export EU free market and intervention grain at Thursday's weekly EU auction hope Brussels will help cover part of the sale as it faces the prospect of a bumper crop in Europe and tough competition from other suppliers.
"Brussels cannot afford to miss the largest world buyer of barley," one trader said, adding that an export subsidy of over 30 Ecus per tonne would be needed.
Saudi Arabia bought the grain at prices ranging from $146 to $158 per tonne, including costs and freight, for delivery between October and December.
Those prices include about $20 in freight and other costs, traders have said.
World barley prices have firmed again from as low as $130 per tonne, FOB, last week on news the Saudis were launching a tender for barley.
Written confirmation of the deal was still pending on Tuesday, but several operators involved in the negotiation said they were told by the Saudis the sale had been clinched.
Saudi Arabia needs 200,000 tonnes for delivery in October.
The European Union is curently the only potential supplier for that period, traders said.
A further 800,000 tonnes of barley is expected to be delivered in November and 400,000 tonnes in the first half of December though there may be delays in shipments to congested Saudi ports.
Of the 1.4 million tonnes purchase, between 800,000 and 900,000 tonnes may come from the EU, over 125,000 tonnes from Turkey and the rest from Canada, the U.S. and Australia.
Traders expect the EU share to be split between intervention and the open market.
In late August Saudi Arabia bought 800,000 tonnes of barley, with some 600,000 tonnes going to the EU.
The Commission helped cover part of that sale with German intervention barley but in recent weeks it has allowed barley exports from the free market.
On September 12 it granted 316,000 tonnes of free market barley at a maximum refund of 24.97 Ecus per tonne.
On September 19 it awarded a further 46,000 tonnes at a refund of 24.99 Ecus, worth around $142 per tonne, FOB.
Among EU producers, France is hoping to sell a large part of its barley crop on world markets, France's grain office ONIC said earlier this month.

Saudi Arabia is one of the importers France hopes to do business with in the new 1996/97 season as ONIC has set an ambitious target of 1.8 million tonnes for French barley exports to non-EU countries this season, against just 221,000 tonnes last year.
French barley into Rouen firmed 10 francs to 880 francs per tonne on Tuesday on news of the Saudi purchase.
